name: Seated Band Ankle Dorsiflexion
movementDefinition: Sit comfortably with the working foot resting on a board beneath an elastic band affixed to that board. Set a physical stop at the working ankle's comfortable dorsiflexion limit. Begin from the self-selected resting position with the sole on the board and hold the selected knee posture still. Dorsiflex the ankle to lift the foot toward the shin until reaching the stop, without deliberately turning the foot inward or outward or extending the toes to create the repetition. Return under control until the sole touches the board, then repeat before changing sides.

name: Standing Unilateral Machine Calf Raise
movementDefinition: Stand in a unilateral calf-raise machine with the working forefoot neutral on the platform, the shoulder beneath the load pad, and the knee held extended. Keep the hip, pelvis, spine, knee, and foot orientation still; raise the heel through ankle plantarflexion, then lower under control without bending the knee or curling the toes.

name: Seated Unilateral Machine Calf Raise
movementDefinition: Sit in a unilateral calf-raise machine with the working forefoot neutral on the platform, the distal thigh beneath the load pad, and the knee held near 90 degrees of flexion. Keep the hip, pelvis, spine, knee, and foot orientation still; raise the heel through ankle plantarflexion, then lower under control without extending the knee or curling the toes.

name: Stable Forearm Plank
movementDefinition: Set both forearms on a stable floor with the elbows below the shoulders and the upper arms perpendicular to the floor, then support the lower body on both feet. Hold the spine, pelvis, hips, and knees in one neutral straight line for the prescribed duration while resisting the tendency of the lower back to sag; do not turn the hold into a crunch, hip lift, reach, or limb movement.

name: Side Plank
movementDefinition: Lie on one side and support the body on that forearm and elbow with the shoulder and elbow at the reviewed 90-degree angles. Extend both legs, place the top foot in front of the lower foot, place the free hand on the opposite shoulder, and lift into a straight line from shoulder through hip to feet. Hold the spine, pelvis, and hips still for the prescribed duration, then repeat on the other side without adding a hip dip, row, or leg movement.

name: Feet-Together Band Pallof Hold
movementDefinition: Attach a band to a side pulley so its line of pull is horizontal, stand side-on with the feet together on a stable floor, and hold the handle in both hands at shoulder height. Extend both elbows so the arms are perpendicular to the torso, choose a tension you can control, and hold for the prescribed duration without letting the spine or pelvis rotate. Repeat with the anchor on the other side; do not turn the hold into a repeated press.

name: Barbell Back Squat
movementDefinition: Stand with the heels about hip-width apart and a straight barbell resting securely across the upper back. Hold the bar with both hands in a pronated grip, brace the trunk, and keep both feet planted. Flex the hips and knees while allowing the ankles to dorsiflex until the upper thighs reach approximately parallel to the floor. Without sitting on a box, bouncing, or deliberately using spinal motion to create the repetition, extend the hips and knees and plantarflex the ankles back toward standing while maintaining control of the free bar; the exact lumbar path is not standardized.

name: Barbell Front Squat
movementDefinition: Stand with the heels about hip-width apart and a straight barbell supported across the anterior deltoids and clavicles in a clean grip. Brace the trunk, keep the elbows lifted, and keep both feet planted. Flex the hips and knees while allowing the ankles to dorsiflex until the upper thighs reach approximately parallel to the floor. Without sitting on a support, bouncing, or deliberately using spinal motion to create the repetition, extend the hips and knees and plantarflex the ankles back toward standing while keeping the free bar balanced on the front rack; the exact lumbar path is not standardized.

name: Flat Dumbbell Fly
movementDefinition: Lie supine on a flat bench with one dumbbell over each shoulder, palms facing each other, and the elbows held in a fixed slight bend. Lower the upper arms outward at shoulder height, then horizontally adduct them to bring the dumbbells back over the chest without pressing, bending the elbows, or deliberately protracting the scapulae.

name: Standing Band Fly
movementDefinition: Stand between the anchored ends of an elastic band with the upper arms held at shoulder height, palms facing inward, and the elbows in a fixed slight bend. Brace the trunk and horizontally adduct the upper arms until the hands meet in front of the chest, then return under control without pressing, bending the elbows, or turning scapular protraction into the prime action.

name: Decline Barbell Bench Press
movementDefinition: Secure the legs on a bench declined 15 degrees and lie with the eyes below the racked bar. Lower the bar under control toward the lower-chest line, then press through shoulder horizontal adduction and elbow extension while keeping the torso and shoulders supported.

name: Decline Dumbbell Bench Press
movementDefinition: Secure the legs on a bench declined 15 degrees and begin with one dumbbell beside each lower-chest line. Keep each forearm under its load, press the dumbbells upward and slightly inward to elbow extension, then lower them under control without turning the repetition into a fly.

name: Decline Smith Machine Bench Press
movementDefinition: Set a decline bench to 15 degrees and position it so the Smith bar descends toward the lower chest without forcing the shoulders forward. Lower the bar along the rails under control, then press to elbow extension while keeping the torso and shoulders supported.

name: Decline Machine Chest Press
movementDefinition: Adjust the seat so the handles begin beside the lower chest and follow an approximately 15-degree downward path relative to a horizontal press. Keep the torso against the pad, press the handles forward and inward to elbow extension, then return under control.

name: Seated 45-Degree Cable Pulldown
movementDefinition: Sit on a flat bench facing the reviewed high cable with both feet on the floor and no thigh restraint. Take a wider-than-shoulder-width pronated grip on the straight bar and begin with the elbows extended and the arms on the source-prescribed 45-degree line. Keep the head straight and the core engaged, then pull the bar to touch the chest by extending the shoulders and flexing the elbows. Allow the scapulae to move naturally without prescribing retraction or rotation as a separate action, and return slowly to the same 45-degree start without adding shoulder adduction or axial rotation, leaning to propel the bar, or using the lower body. The source tested both 10% and 25% of bodyweight; replace the representative 35 lb/15 kg seed with the actual selected cable load.

name: Bar Dip
movementDefinition: Support the full body above fixed dip bars with no foot contact. Lower under control by flexing the elbows and allowing the shoulders to extend behind the torso only to a self-selected controlled depth. Press back up through shoulder flexion toward neutral and elbow extension without swinging, kicking, or forcing a scapular action that the reviewed trials did not measure.

name: Ring Dip
movementDefinition: Support the full body above two independent rings with no foot contact. Keep the rings controlled beside the torso, lower by flexing the elbows and allowing the shoulders to extend behind the torso to a self-selected controlled depth, then return through shoulder flexion toward neutral and elbow extension without kipping or using the legs.

name: Bodyweight Forward Lunge
movementDefinition: Stand upright with both feet supporting you and cross the arms over the upper body. Step forward with the selected lead foot, land with the whole foot in contact, and lower under control for three seconds to full self-selected depth. Keep the lead foot planted, then extend the lead hip and knee and move the lead ankle from its dorsiflexed bottom position toward standing over two seconds. Step the lead foot back to the bilateral start to complete the repetition. Finish the set on the selected side, then repeat with the other lead leg.

name: Bodyweight Reverse Lunge
movementDefinition: Stand upright with both feet supporting you and cross the arms over the upper body. Keep the selected front foot planted and step the contralateral foot backward. After the rear foot lands, lower under control for three seconds to full self-selected depth without moving the selected front foot. Extend the selected front hip and knee and move its ankle from the dorsiflexed bottom position toward standing over two seconds, then bring the rear foot forward to the bilateral start. Finish the set with the same selected front leg, then repeat on the other side.

name: Single-Arm Supinated Cable Triceps Pushdown
movementDefinition: Stand at a high cable and hold a single handle with the working forearm supinated. Keep the upper arm alongside the torso and the wrist neutral; extend the elbow from about 90 degrees to straight, then return under control without moving the shoulder or rotating the forearm.

name: Single-Arm Pronated Cable Triceps Pushdown
movementDefinition: Stand at a high cable and hold a single handle with the working forearm pronated. Keep the upper arm alongside the torso and the wrist neutral; extend the elbow from about 90 degrees to straight, then return under control without moving the shoulder or rotating the forearm.

name: Single-Arm Overhead Cable Triceps Extension
movementDefinition: Stand with one arm held overhead and the forearm supinated while a cable opposes elbow extension. Keep the upper arm, wrist, torso, and lower body still; extend the elbow from about 90 degrees to straight, then return under control.

name: Seated Single-Arm Overhead Dumbbell Triceps Extension
movementDefinition: Sit upright without back support and hold one dumbbell with a neutral forearm and the upper arm overhead. Keep the upper arm and torso still; flex the elbow to lower the dumbbell, then extend through the available range without rotating the forearm.

name: Single-Arm Lying Dumbbell Triceps Extension
movementDefinition: Lie supine on a bench with one neutral-grip dumbbell held over the chest and the upper arm at 90 degrees of shoulder flexion. Hold the upper arm still, lower the dumbbell by flexing the elbow, then extend the elbow through the available range.

name: Supinated Straight-Bar Cable Curl
movementDefinition: Stand facing a low cable while holding a straight bar with both forearms supinated. Keep the upper arms parallel to the torso, wrists neutral, and body still; flex the elbows through the available range, then lower the bar under control without rotating the forearms.

name: Neutral-Grip Rope Cable Curl
movementDefinition: Stand facing a low cable while holding the rope ends with both forearms neutral. Keep the upper arms parallel to the torso, wrists neutral, and body still; flex the elbows through the available range, then return under control without rotating the forearms.

name: Pronated Straight-Bar Cable Curl
movementDefinition: Stand facing a low cable while holding a straight bar with both forearms pronated. Keep the upper arms parallel to the torso, wrists neutral, and body still; flex the elbows through the available range, then lower the bar under control without rotating the forearms.

name: Two-Dumbbell Farmer Carry
movementDefinition: Log the weight of one dumbbell, not the combined pair. Hold one equal-weight dumbbell in each hand with the upper arms at the sides, neutral humeral and forearm rotation, palms facing the thighs, no straps or hooks, and the elbows held extended beside the torso. Walk continuously forward on a level surface for the prescribed duration while keeping the shoulders controlled and the trunk upright without turning, marching in place, or converting the carry into another exercise.

name: Repetitive Grip-Trainer Close
movementDefinition: Use one 30 kg-rated grip trainer in one hand and complete 30 repeated grip cycles without assistance from the other hand. Close and release the fingers under control, but do not assume a handles-touching endpoint, fixed cadence, or prescribed wrist, forearm, elbow, or body posture: the reviewed study did not report those details. The source used three sets; log each set separately and repeat with the other hand. Enter no lifted weight because the trainer's rating is non-comparable product resistance.

name: Seated Dumbbell Forearm Pronation
movementDefinition: Sit with the working shoulder relaxed, the elbow flexed about 90 degrees, and the forearm supported on a table. Begin fully supinated while holding a plate-loaded dumbbell vertically, rotate only the forearm until the thumb points upward at neutral, and return under control without moving the wrist, elbow, shoulder, or torso.

name: Seated Dumbbell Forearm Supination
movementDefinition: Sit with the working shoulder relaxed, the elbow flexed about 90 degrees, and the forearm supported on a table. Begin fully pronated while holding a plate-loaded dumbbell vertically, rotate only the forearm until the thumb points upward at neutral, and return under control without moving the wrist, elbow, shoulder, or torso.

name: Pressure-Biofeedback Side-Lying Hip Abduction
movementDefinition: Lie on one side on a treatment table with the working leg on top, the hip neutral in flexion-extension and axial rotation, the lower leg flexed for stability, and a cuff weight secured just above the working ankle. Place a pressure-biofeedback unit beneath the trunk, inflate it to 40 mmHg, and keep it between 35 and 45 mmHg while a horizontal contact band marks 35 degrees of abduction. Keep the pelvis and spine still, the working knee straight, and the toes pointing forward. Raise the straight top leg in the frontal plane until it contacts the endpoint band, then lower it under control without rolling the pelvis or turning the toes upward.

name: Supported Standing Band Hip Adduction
movementDefinition: Stand upright on the support leg while holding a stable external support with both hands and secure an elastic band around the working ankle from the side. Place the straight working leg in maximal comfortable abduction with tension already in the band and hold it at the same slight posterior hip posture used at the endpoint. Keep the pelvis still, the working knee straight, and both sets of toes pointing forward as you draw the working thigh medially without swinging it farther backward, finishing one foot-width lateral to and about half a foot-length behind the stance foot. Return under control along the same strictly frontal path, then repeat before changing sides.

name: Prone Table Bent-Knee Hip Extension
movementDefinition: Lie prone with the torso and pelvis supported on a table and the working thigh hanging beyond its edge. Hold the working knee at 90 degrees and begin with the hip at the reviewed 30-degree flexed position. Keep the pelvis and spine still while extending the hip until the thigh reaches the reviewed 5-degree extension endpoint, then lower the thigh under control without changing the knee angle or turning the repetition into spinal or pelvic motion.

name: Therapist-Held Supine Band Hip External Rotation
movementDefinition: Lie supine on a treatment table with both thighs supported over the wedge so both hips remain at 30 degrees of flexion and both knees remain flexed. Secure the elastic band at the working ankle. The therapist stabilizes the working knee against the support and holds the other end of the band so it opposes external hip rotation. Keep the pelvis and spine still and begin with the working hip in neutral rotation. Move the working lower leg against the band until the hip reaches the middle of its available external-rotation range, then return to neutral under control without lifting or turning the working thigh. Complete the prescribed repetitions before changing sides.

name: Bodyweight Active Straight-Leg Raise
movementDefinition: Lie supine with the torso and pelvis supported on a table and both legs extended. Keep the nonworking leg supported and the working knee straight. Raise the working leg by flexing the hip until reaching your active end range, then lower it under control. Keep the effort centered on the working hip without deliberately adding spinal, pelvic, or knee motion.

name: 25% Body-Mass Barbell Good Morning
aliases: Barbell Good Morning at 25% Body Mass
movementDefinition: Stand upright with the feet approximately shoulder-width apart and naturally turned slightly outward. Place a free bar securely across the posterior shoulder and upper-back surface in a comfortable hand position, keep the head aligned with the spine, brace the trunk, and keep both feet planted. Replace the representative 45-pound or 20-kilogram seed with external barbell load equal to 25 percent of your body mass. Hinge to the deepest position that preserves the reviewed natural-spine technique, then return to standing by extending the hips and spine at the same normal speed used for the descent. Keep the knees near straight while allowing the small nondefining excursion measured in the reviewed fixture, and retain the bar on the body between all eight repetitions.

name: Seated Flywheel Hip Internal Rotation
movementDefinition: Sit on a hydraulic treatment table set 75 cm above the floor with both hips and knees flexed to 90 degrees, both feet suspended, the hands crossed over the opposite shoulders, and the pelvis neutral. Secure the working distal femur with one belt and the pelvis at both anterior superior iliac spines with two belts. Connect the working ankle brace to the Conic Power Move cable by carabiner, using the horizontally wall-fixed flywheel 7 cm above the floor, its upper-middle sliding-frame position, the reported 460-g attached load and 15-cm axis distance, and a cable length matched to the maximum active hip-rotation range. Internally rotate the working femur relative to the fixed pelvis as fast as possible, moving the lower leg outward, then return while counteracting the generated flywheel inertia. Keep the knee angle fixed and do not move the pelvis, spine, or thigh outside the hip-rotation path. After two sets of ten progressively harder warm-up repetitions, perform three progressive repetitions and seven high-intensity work repetitions, then repeat the reviewed setup for the other leg as a separately logged set.

name: Barbell Hip Thrust
movementDefinition: Sit with the upper back anchored against a 35.5-centimeter bench and a padded barbell across the pelvis. Plant the feet at shoulder width so the knees finish near 90 degrees, steady the bar with a supinated grip, and raise the pelvis until the hips reach neutral. Lower until the plates return to the floor without adding deliberate spinal extension or abduction.

name: Barbell Glute Bridge
movementDefinition: Lie with the upper torso anchored on the floor, a padded barbell across the pelvis, and the feet shoulder-width apart with the reviewed flexed-knee setup. Steady the bar with a supinated grip and raise the pelvis until the hips reach neutral and the knees finish near 115 degrees of flexion. Lower until the plates return to the floor without shifting the upper torso or adding deliberate spinal extension or abduction.

name: Barbell Bench Press
movementDefinition: Lie on a flat bench with the eyes beneath the racked bar and the feet planted. Lower the bar under control toward the lower chest, then press it upward through shoulder horizontal adduction and elbow extension.

name: Dumbbell Bench Press
movementDefinition: Lie on a flat bench with one dumbbell beside each side of the chest. Press both dumbbells upward until the elbows are extended, then lower them under control while keeping the forearms beneath the loads.

name: Neutral-Grip Dumbbell Bench Press
movementDefinition: Lie on a flat bench holding the dumbbells beside the chest with the palms facing each other. Keep the elbows closer to the torso, press to elbow extension, and lower under control without changing the neutral grip.

name: Smith Machine Bench Press
movementDefinition: Position a flat bench so the Smith bar descends toward the lower chest. Unrack the bar, lower it under control along the rails, then press to elbow extension without allowing the shoulders to lift from the bench.

name: Machine Chest Press
movementDefinition: Adjust the seat so the neutral-grip handles begin beside the mid-chest with the forearms aligned to the machine path. Keep the torso against the pad, press the handles forward and slightly inward along the converging lever path to elbow extension, then return under control.

name: Standing Cable Chest Press
movementDefinition: Stand between two chest-height cable handles in a stable staggered stance with the palms facing inward. Press both handles forward while allowing controlled scapular protraction, then return until the elbows pass slightly behind the torso without rotating the trunk.

name: Single-Arm Cable Chest Press
movementDefinition: Stand with one chest-height cable handle beside the working-side chest and the palm facing inward. Brace against cable-driven trunk rotation, press through elbow extension and scapular protraction, then return under control before changing sides.

name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Bench Press
movementDefinition: Lie on a flat bench with one dumbbell beside the working-side chest in a neutral grip. Keep the torso square against the unilateral load, press to elbow extension, and lower under control before changing sides.

name: Push-Up
movementDefinition: Begin in a straight-body plank with the hands slightly wider than the shoulders. Lower the chest toward the floor, then press the body away while extending the elbows and allowing the shoulder blades to protract without losing trunk position.

name: Knee Push-Up
movementDefinition: Begin with the knees and hands supporting the body and maintain a straight line from the knees through the shoulders. Lower the chest toward the floor, then press away through elbow extension and controlled scapular protraction.

name: Barbell Floor Press
movementDefinition: Lie on the floor beneath a safely positioned bar with the knees bent. Lower the bar until the upper arms contact the floor without bouncing, pause briefly, then press upward to elbow extension.

name: Dumbbell Floor Press
movementDefinition: Lie on the floor with a dumbbell beside each side of the chest, the palms facing inward, and the knees bent. Lower until the upper arms contact the floor without bouncing, then press both dumbbells upward to elbow extension.

name: Incline Barbell Bench Press
movementDefinition: Set the bench backrest to 30 degrees and lie with the feet planted and eyes below the racked bar. Lower the bar under control toward the upper chest, then press upward through shoulder flexion, horizontal adduction, and elbow extension without lifting the shoulders from the bench.

name: Incline Dumbbell Bench Press
movementDefinition: Set the bench backrest to 30 degrees and lie with one dumbbell beside each upper-chest line. Keep each forearm under its load, press the dumbbells upward and slightly inward to elbow extension, then lower under control without letting the upper arms drift into a vertical shoulder-press path.

name: Incline Smith Machine Bench Press
movementDefinition: Set the bench backrest to 30 degrees and position it so the Smith bar descends toward the upper chest without forcing the shoulders forward. Lower the bar along the rails under control, then press to elbow extension while keeping the torso and shoulders supported.

name: Incline Machine Chest Press
movementDefinition: Adjust the seat so the handles begin beside the upper chest and follow an approximately 30-degree upward path relative to a horizontal press. Keep the torso against the pad, press the handles forward and upward to elbow extension, then return under control.

name: Reclined Unilateral Machine Leg Extension
movementDefinition: Sit in a unilateral knee-extension machine with the backrest reclined so the hip is held near 40 degrees of flexion, the knee aligned to the lever axis, and the distal shin against the pad. Keep the pelvis, spine, hip, ankle, and foot still; extend the knee from the reviewed flexed start to full extension, then return under control.

name: Upright Unilateral Machine Leg Extension
movementDefinition: Sit upright in a unilateral knee-extension machine with the hip held near 90 degrees of flexion, the knee aligned to the lever axis, and the distal shin against the pad. Keep the pelvis, spine, hip, ankle, and foot still; extend the knee from the reviewed flexed start to full extension, then return under control.

name: Seated Unilateral Machine Leg Curl
movementDefinition: Sit in a unilateral leg-curl machine with the hip held near 90 degrees of flexion, the pelvis secured to the pad, the knee aligned to the lever axis, and the distal lower leg against the pad. Keep the pelvis, spine, hip, ankle, and foot still; flex the knee from full extension to approximately 90 degrees, then return under control.

name: Prone Unilateral Machine Leg Curl
movementDefinition: Lie prone in a unilateral leg-curl machine with the hip held near 30 degrees of flexion, the pelvis secured to the pad, the knee aligned to the lever axis, and the distal lower leg against the pad. Keep the pelvis, spine, hip, ankle, and foot still; flex the knee from full extension to approximately 90 degrees, then return under control.

name: Standing Single-Arm Landmine Press Power Test
movementDefinition: Fix one end of an Olympic bar in a landmine pivot and count the full bar plus every plate as the logged load. For the right arm, stand with the left foot forward and both sets of toes pointing ahead; mirror the stance for the left arm. Fully grip the moving sleeve and begin with it close to the working-side deltoid. Without deliberately driving through the hips, knees, or ankles, press the sleeve through its pivoted arc to a controlled end range, then return it to the shoulder. Perform three power-focused repetitions, log the opposite side separately, and keep the trunk and pelvis controlled without treating them as measured position-held segments.

name: Barbell Push Press
movementDefinition: Stand with the feet about hip-width apart and hold a straight barbell in the front rack with a pronated grip just outside shoulder width. Brace the trunk and make an upright push-press countermovement by flexing the hips and knees while keeping both feet in contact with the floor. Immediately extend the hips, knees, and ankles to propel the bar upward, then press it in front of the head to overhead lockout as the scapulae rotate upward. Finish standing with the elbows extended without dipping under the bar, then lower the bar under control to the front rack.

name: Prone Dumbbell Reverse Fly
movementDefinition: Lie prone on a bench with one dumbbell in each hand, palms facing inward, and the elbows held in a fixed slight bend. Horizontally abduct the upper arms at shoulder height until they align with the torso, keeping the scapulae controlled rather than deliberately retracting them, then lower under control without rowing, bending the elbows, or rotating the shoulders.

name: Standing Band Reverse Fly
movementDefinition: Stand upright holding an elastic band in front of the chest with the palms facing inward and the elbows in a fixed slight bend. Brace the trunk and horizontally abduct the upper arms at shoulder height to stretch the band, keeping the scapulae controlled rather than deliberately retracting them, then return under control without rowing, bending the elbows, or rotating the shoulders.

name: Neutral-Grip Machine Reverse Fly
movementDefinition: Sit facing the reverse-fly machine pad and hold the handles with the palms facing each other, upper arms at shoulder height, and elbows in a fixed slight bend. Follow the lever path to horizontally abduct the shoulders, keeping the scapulae controlled rather than deliberately retracting them, then return under control without rowing, bending the elbows, or adding shoulder rotation.

name: Pronated-Grip Machine Reverse Fly
movementDefinition: Sit facing the reverse-fly machine pad and hold the horizontal handles with the palms facing down, upper arms at shoulder height, and elbows in a fixed slight bend. Follow the lever path to horizontally abduct the shoulders, keeping the scapulae controlled rather than deliberately retracting them, then return under control without rowing, bending the elbows, or deliberately externally rotating the shoulders.

name: Standing Band Scapular Depression
movementDefinition: Stand tall holding the overhead-anchored band beside the working thigh with the elbow extended and the band just taut. Lower the shoulder girdle by depressing the scapula against the band for two seconds, then return for two seconds without bending the elbow, moving the glenohumeral joint, leaning the trunk, or moving the neck. Rest five seconds between repetitions.

name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Shrug
movementDefinition: Stand tall holding one dumbbell beside the torso with the elbow extended and the thumb pointing forward. Elevate the working scapula toward the ear while keeping the humerus at the side and allowing its measured upward rotation, then lower under control without rolling the shoulder, bending the elbow, moving the neck, or leaning the trunk.

name: Bilateral 30-Degree Stabilization Shrug
movementDefinition: Stand with the feet shoulder-width apart and both arms held at 30 degrees of frontal-plane abduction. Lightly contact the radial borders of the wrists against the plastic guides, use the inclinometer to retain the arm angle, and have a partner stabilize the chin and upper thorax. Shrug both scapulae to the individual maximum-height target bars, hold the top position for five seconds, then lower slowly without bending the elbows, moving the neck or trunk, or adding external load. Perform two source-prescribed trials. The catalog's upward-rotation action reflects the greater angle measured immediately after this condition, not a continuously tracked dynamic angle.

name: Supine Dumbbell Scapular Punch
movementDefinition: Lie supine with one dumbbell held vertically above the shoulder, the upper arm fixed at 90 degrees of forward elevation, and the elbow extended. Without bending the elbow or flexing the shoulder, reach the load toward the ceiling by moving the scapula anterolaterally around the thorax, then return under control without adding a press.

name: Standing Band Scapular Retraction
movementDefinition: Stand facing the low anterior band anchor and hold the working arm near 80 degrees of forward flexion with the elbow extended and the band just taut. Draw the scapula posteriorly toward the spine against the band for two seconds, then return for two seconds without bending the elbow, dynamically moving the glenohumeral joint, elevating the shoulder, turning the trunk, or moving the neck. Rest five seconds between repetitions.

name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Lateral Raise
movementDefinition: Stand upright with one dumbbell beside the thigh, the humerus neutrally rotated, and the elbow held nearly extended. Raise the upper arm directly out to the side in the frontal plane from the side to shoulder height without shrugging, leaning, or using lower-body drive, then lower it under control.

name: Single-Arm Cable Lateral Raise
movementDefinition: Stand upright holding one cable handle with the pulley aligned approximately with the working hand in the arm-at-side start. Keep the humerus neutrally rotated and the elbow nearly extended while raising the upper arm directly out to the side in the frontal plane to shoulder height, then lower it without shrugging, leaning, or using lower-body drive.

name: Barbell Pullover
movementDefinition: Lie supine along a flat bench and hold a straight bar over the chest with a shoulder-width pronated grip and nearly extended elbows. Keeping the elbow angle fixed, lower the bar behind the head until the upper arms reach the reviewed overhead zone, then extend the shoulders to return the bar over the chest without turning the repetition into an elbow-extension movement.

name: Shoulder-Width Straight-Arm Cable Pulldown
movementDefinition: Stand facing a high cable and hold a straight bar at shoulder width with a pronated grip and nearly extended elbows. Begin with the hands in the reviewed overhead zone, brace the trunk, and keep the elbow angle fixed while extending the shoulders to bring the bar to the thighs; return overhead under control without rowing or bending the elbows.

name: Wide-Grip Straight-Arm Cable Pulldown
movementDefinition: Stand facing a high cable and hold a straight bar wider than shoulder width with a pronated grip and nearly extended elbows. Begin with the hands in the reviewed overhead zone, brace the trunk, and keep the elbow angle fixed while extending the shoulders to bring the bar to the thighs; return overhead under control without rowing or bending the elbows.

name: Barbell Bent-Over Row
movementDefinition: Stand holding a barbell with a shoulder-width pronated grip, hinge at the hips until the torso is inclined, and brace without changing the torso angle. Pull the bar toward the lower ribs while the elbows travel back near the torso, then lower it under control.

name: Underhand Barbell Row
movementDefinition: Hold a barbell with a shoulder-width supinated grip and maintain a strict hip hinge with the trunk braced. Keep the elbows tucked, pull the bar toward the lower torso without standing up, and lower it under control.

name: Pendlay Row
movementDefinition: Set a barbell on the floor and take a shoulder-width pronated grip while holding a strict hip hinge. Pull the bar toward the lower ribs without extending the hips or spine, lower it to a complete floor reset, and rebrace before the next repetition.

name: Dumbbell Bent-Over Row
movementDefinition: Hold a dumbbell in each hand with the palms facing inward and establish a strict hip hinge. Pull both dumbbells toward the sides of the lower torso while keeping the elbows close, then lower them without changing the trunk angle.

name: One-Arm Dumbbell Row
movementDefinition: Place the opposite hand and knee on a bench while the working-side foot stays planted, then hold one dumbbell with a neutral grip. Keep the pelvis square, pull the elbow toward the hip without rotating the torso, and lower under control.

name: Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row
movementDefinition: Lie prone with the chest supported on an incline bench and hold two dumbbells with neutral grips. Let the shoulder blades move around the rib cage, pull the elbows toward the lower torso, and lower the dumbbells under control.

name: Seated Cable Row
movementDefinition: Sit upright at a low cable station holding a narrow neutral attachment, with the torso unsupported and braced. Pull the handle toward the lower ribs while keeping the elbows tucked, then return until the shoulder blades move forward under control.

name: Single-Arm Seated Cable Row
movementDefinition: Sit upright at a low cable station and hold one handle with a neutral grip. Brace the trunk and keep the pelvis square as the working elbow travels toward the hip, then return the arm forward without rotating the torso.

name: Chest-Supported Machine Row
movementDefinition: Sit at a linked-arm lever-row machine with the chest against the pad and hold the handles with neutral grips. Allow normal scapular motion, drive the elbows toward the lower torso without lifting the chest from the pad, and return the linked lever under control.

name: Single-Arm Chest-Supported Machine Row
movementDefinition: Sit against the chest pad of an independent-arm lever-row machine and hold one handle with a neutral grip. Keep the pelvis and chest square, pull the working elbow toward the lower torso, and return the lever without twisting away from the pad.

name: Smith Machine Bent-Over Row
movementDefinition: Set the Smith bar near knee height, take a shoulder-width pronated grip, and establish a strict hip hinge beneath the rail path. Pull the bar toward the lower ribs without changing the torso angle, then lower it along the rails under control.

name: Inverted Row
movementDefinition: Lie beneath a fixed straight bar with a shoulder-width pronated grip, feet on the floor, and the body held approximately parallel to the floor. Keep a straight line from shoulders through heels, pull the chest toward the bar through a modest scapular upper-arm path, and lower under control.

name: Standing Cable External Rotation
movementDefinition: Stand side-on with the cable anchored across the body, hold the working upper arm beside the torso with the elbow flexed about 90 degrees, and rotate the forearm away from the abdomen. Return under control without moving the elbow, retracting the shoulder blade, or turning the torso.

name: Standing Band External Rotation
movementDefinition: Stand side-on with the band anchored across the body and a towel roll between the working upper arm and torso. Keep the elbow flexed about 90 degrees, rotate the forearm away from the abdomen against the band, and return without moving the elbow, shoulder blade, or torso.

name: Side-Lying Dumbbell External Rotation
movementDefinition: Lie on the nonworking side on a flat bench with a towel roll between the working upper arm and torso, the elbow flexed about 90 degrees, and a dumbbell held above the abdomen. Rotate the forearm toward the ceiling and lower it under control without lifting the upper arm, rolling the torso, or retracting the shoulder blade.

name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Front Raise
movementDefinition: Stand upright with one dumbbell beside the thigh, the humerus neutrally rotated, and the elbow held nearly extended. Raise the upper arm directly forward from the side to shoulder height without bending the elbow, shrugging, leaning, or using lower-body drive, then lower it under control.

name: Wide-Grip Barbell Rear-Delt Row
movementDefinition: Hold a barbell with a wide pronated grip and maintain a strict hip hinge. Pull toward the upper chest while the elbows travel out at shoulder height, retract the shoulder blades without depressing them, and lower the bar without extending the hips or spine.

name: Chest-Supported Dumbbell Rear-Delt Row
movementDefinition: Lie prone with the chest supported on an incline bench and hold two dumbbells with neutral grips. Keep the forearms beneath the elbows as the upper arms travel out at shoulder height, retract the shoulder blades, and lower the dumbbells under control without lifting the chest.

name: Wide-Grip Seated Cable Rear-Delt Row
movementDefinition: Sit upright at a shoulder-height cable and hold a wide straight attachment with a pronated grip. Brace the unsupported torso, pull toward the upper chest with the elbows flared at shoulder height, retract the shoulder blades, and return under control.

name: Single-Arm Seated Cable Rear-Delt Row
movementDefinition: Sit upright at a shoulder-height cable and hold one handle with a neutral grip. Keep the pelvis and torso square as the working elbow travels out and back at shoulder height, retract the working-side scapula, and return without rotating the trunk.

name: Chest-Supported Machine Rear-Delt Row
movementDefinition: Sit at a horizontal lever-row machine with the chest against the pad and take the wide pronated handles. Pull with both elbows out at shoulder height while allowing the shoulder blades to retract over the rib cage, then return the linked lever under control.

name: Single-Arm Chest-Supported Machine Rear-Delt Row
movementDefinition: Sit against the chest pad of an independent-arm horizontal lever row and hold one neutral handle. Keep the pelvis and chest square while the working elbow travels out and back at shoulder height, retract the scapula, and return the lever without twisting.

name: Standing Cable Internal Rotation
movementDefinition: Stand side-on with the cable anchored outside the working shoulder and a towel roll between the upper arm and torso. Keep the elbow flexed about 90 degrees, rotate the forearm across the abdomen, and return under control without moving the elbow, protracting the shoulder blade, or turning the torso.

name: Standing Band Internal Rotation
movementDefinition: Stand side-on with the band anchored outside the working shoulder and a towel roll between the upper arm and torso. Keep the elbow flexed about 90 degrees, rotate the forearm across the abdomen against the band, and return without moving the elbow, protracting the shoulder blade, or turning the torso.

name: MedX Isolated Lumbar Extension
movementDefinition: Sit in the MedX lumbar-extension machine with the thighs perpendicular to the seat. Tighten the thigh restraint, secure the distal-femur restraint just above the patella, tighten the footboard, and maintain contact with the rolling upper-pelvis restraint. Apply extension force only to the posterior upper-torso resistance pad. From the machine's 72-degree full-lumbar-flexion reference, extend for at least two seconds to its 0-degree full-extension reference, hold one second, then return for at least four seconds without lifting or rotating the pelvis or driving with the hips.

name: 30-Degree Curl-Up
movementDefinition: Lie supine in a stable lower-body position with the pelvis held still. Begin with the trunk resting on the floor, then flex the spine to curl the head, shoulders, and upper trunk through the reviewed 30-degree range without using hip motion. Return to the supine start under control without turning the repetition into a full sit-up.

name: Fixed-Leg Side-Lying Lateral Trunk Lift
movementDefinition: Lie on one side with the trunk resting on the floor, cross the upper foot over the lower leg, and have the crossed upper foot fixed securely without assuming a particular device. As a catalog coaching standard beyond the measured source, hold the pelvis and hip still rather than driving the lift from the hip. Laterally flex the spine to lift the upper body to the 30-degree trunk-elevation endpoint; this is not a segmental lumbar-angle prescription. Return to the side-lying start under control, then complete the same separately logged work in the opposite lateral-flexion direction.

name: Seated Machine Torso Twist
movementDefinition: Sit in a horizontal torso-twist machine with the feet behind the ankle rollers, the shoulder pads in contact, and both hands holding the separate handles at shoulder height. Hold the pelvis against the seat and keep the hips and legs still. For one logged direction, begin rotated left, drive the shoulder pads from left to right in a controlled motion, stop at the largest comfortable torso-rotation endpoint, and return to the left-rotated start under control. Then reset the machine and perform the same prescribed work from right to left as a separately logged direction. The right-to-left direction is a mirrored training adaptation; do not alternate directions within a repetition.

name: Barbell Split Squat
movementDefinition: Place a barbell securely across the upper back and hold it with both hands in a pronated grip. Take a fixed sagittal split stance approximately equal to your greater-trochanter-to-lateral-malleolus leg length, with the lead foot flat and the trail forefoot on the floor; the reviewed study did not report a precise foot landmark for this taped condition. Keep the torso erect and both foot contacts fixed. Lower until the lead thigh is approximately parallel to the floor, then extend the lead hip and knee and move the lead ankle from its bottom-position dorsiflexion toward the split-standing angle. Finish in the same split stance without stepping between repetitions.

name: 21 cm Bodyweight Forward Step-Up
movementDefinition: Stand facing a platform exactly 21 centimeters above the lower floor with the lead foot placed fully on top and the trail foot on the lower floor. Shift onto the lead leg without pushing or hopping from the trail leg. Extend the lead hip and knee and move the lead ankle from its dorsiflexed lower position toward the standing angle until the trail foot reaches the platform beside the lead foot. Pause briefly in bilateral standing. Shift back onto the lead leg, return the trail foot to the lower floor, then step the lead foot down beside it to complete the repetition. Replace the same lead foot fully on the platform before the next repetition, and switch lead sides after the set.

name: Single-Dumbbell Suitcase Carry
movementDefinition: Log the weight of the single dumbbell. Hold it at one side with the upper arm at the side, neutral humeral and forearm rotation, the palm facing the thigh, no straps or hooks, and the elbow held extended beside the torso. Walk continuously forward on a level surface for the prescribed duration while resisting the dumbbell's side-bending tendency without forcing the spine motionless. Log the other side as well; do not turn, march in place, walk backward, or lean deliberately to create repetitions.

name: Standing Low-Cable Upright Row
movementDefinition: Stand at the reviewed low cable with the feet shoulder-width apart and the knees slightly flexed. Hold the straight bar with both hands in the source-shown overhand spacing, keep the torso upright, and engage the core. Pull the bar vertically while flexing the elbows and elevating the upper arms through the mixed flexion-abduction corridor, keeping the elbows slightly above the hands. Stop when the elbows reach shoulder height, then return slowly under control without shrugging as a separate action, retracting the scapulae, rotating the upper arms deliberately, leaning the torso, or adding lower-body drive.

name: Standing Barbell Overhead Press
movementDefinition: Stand with the feet about hip-width apart and hold the bar at the upper chest with a pronated grip just outside shoulder width. Brace the trunk without leaning back, keep the hips and knees motionless, and press the bar overhead as the scapulae rotate upward. Move the head only enough to clear the bar, finish with the elbows extended and the bar balanced over the midfoot, then lower under control to the upper chest.

name: Standing Dumbbell Overhead Press
movementDefinition: Stand with the feet about hip-width apart and hold one dumbbell at each shoulder with the palms facing forward and the elbows slightly forward of the torso. Brace the trunk and keep the hips and knees motionless. Press both dumbbells overhead along independent front-scapular paths without rotating the grips or leaning back, allowing the scapulae to rotate upward. Finish with the elbows extended and the loads balanced over the body, then lower under control to shoulder height.

name: Single-Arm Standing Dumbbell Overhead Press
movementDefinition: Stand with the feet about hip-width apart and hold one dumbbell at the working-side shoulder with the palm facing forward and the elbow slightly forward of the torso. Brace the trunk, keep the pelvis level and the torso facing forward, and keep the hips and knees motionless. Press the dumbbell overhead along a front-scapular path without rotating the grip, leaning sideways or back, or twisting the torso, allowing the working scapula to rotate upward. Finish with the elbow extended and the load balanced over the body, then lower under control before changing sides.

name: Seated Dumbbell Overhead Press
movementDefinition: Set the bench backrest to about 85 degrees and sit with the pelvis and upper torso supported and the feet planted. Hold one dumbbell at each shoulder with the palms facing forward and the elbows slightly forward of the torso. Press both dumbbells overhead along independent front-scapular paths without rotating the grips, pushing through the legs, or lifting the torso from the bench. Allow the scapulae to rotate upward even though the backrest limits their translation, finish with the elbows extended, and lower under control to shoulder height.

name: Seated Barbell Overhead Press
movementDefinition: Set a bench backrest to about 80 degrees inside a rack and sit with the pelvis and upper torso supported and the feet planted. Unrack the bar at the upper chest with a pronated grip just outside shoulder width. Press the bar overhead in front of the head without pushing through the legs or lifting the torso from the bench, allowing the scapulae to rotate upward. Finish with the elbows extended, then lower the bar under control to the upper chest.

name: Unsupported Seated Dumbbell Overhead Press
aliases: Seated Dumbbell Press Without Back Support
movementDefinition: Sit upright on a flat bench without a backrest, plant the feet, and hold one dumbbell at each shoulder with the palms facing forward. Brace the trunk so the ribs stay stacked over the pelvis, then press both dumbbells overhead along independent front-scapular paths without leaning back, pushing through the legs, or rotating the grips. Finish with the elbows extended and lower under control to shoulder height.

name: Single-Arm Seated Dumbbell Overhead Press
movementDefinition: Set the bench backrest to about 75 degrees and sit with the upper torso and pelvis supported and the feet planted. Hold one dumbbell at the working-side shoulder with the palm facing inward. Press it overhead along a front-scapular path without rotating the grip, pushing through the legs, twisting, or leaning sideways, while keeping both sides of the pelvis in contact with the bench. Finish with the elbow extended, lower under control, and repeat on the other side.

name: Single-Arm Standing Kettlebell Overhead Press
movementDefinition: Stand with the feet about shoulder-width apart and rack one kettlebell at the working-side shoulder with a neutral wrist and the bell resting in the standard bell-down position against the forearm. Brace the trunk and keep the hips and knees motionless. Press the kettlebell overhead along a front-scapular path without letting it rotate bottom-up, leaning, or twisting. Finish with the elbow extended and the forearm vertical, then lower under control to the rack before changing sides.

name: Seated Smith Machine Overhead Press
movementDefinition: Place an upright bench under the Smith bar so the rails keep the bar in front of the head, set the backrest to about 85 degrees, and sit with the torso supported and feet planted. Unhook the bar at the upper chest with a pronated grip just outside shoulder width. Press along the rails without pushing through the legs or lifting from the bench, finish with the elbows extended, then lower under control and rehook securely.

name: Machine Shoulder Press
movementDefinition: Adjust the seat so the neutral handles begin near shoulder height and sit with the pelvis and upper torso against the machine pad and the feet planted. Press both lever arms overhead along their converging front paths without pushing through the legs or lifting from the pad. Finish with the elbows extended without forcing the shoulders forward, then return the handles under control.

name: Wall-Supported Strict Handstand Push-Up
movementDefinition: Place the inversion stand ten centimeters from a wall with its hand supports twenty centimeters wider than shoulder breadth and a fifteen-centimeter sponge centered beneath the head. Kick to inversion and let only the feet touch the wall gently. Lower until the head contacts the sponge, then press to full elbow and shoulder extension without collapsing at the waist, bending the knees, kipping, or using the wall for propulsion. The reviewed test counts maximum valid repetitions in forty seconds; five reps is only the catalog's editable starting seed. The source did not measure joint, scapular, or muscle actions, so this record transparently inherits the reviewed vertical-press mechanics and role policy rather than claiming direct dynamic action evidence.

name: Pull-Up
movementDefinition: Hang from a fixed bar with a pronated shoulder-width grip, straight elbows, and a braced trunk. Pull the body upward by driving the elbows down until the chin clears the bar, without swinging or using the hips or legs, then lower under control to a full hang.

name: Chin-Up
movementDefinition: Hang from a fixed bar with a supinated shoulder-width grip, straight elbows, and a braced trunk. Pull the body upward by driving the elbows down until the chin clears the bar, without swinging or lower-body drive, then return under control to a full hang.

name: Neutral-Grip Pull-Up
movementDefinition: Hang from parallel handles with the palms facing each other, straight elbows, and the trunk braced. Pull the body upward by driving the elbows down until the chin clears the handles, keep the lower body motionless, and lower under control to a full hang.

name: Wide-Grip Pull-Up
movementDefinition: Hang from a fixed bar with a pronated grip wider than the shoulders, straight elbows, and a braced trunk. Pull in the front/scapular path until the chin clears the bar without swinging or lower-body drive, then lower under control to a full hang.

name: Assisted Pull-Up Machine
movementDefinition: Set the assistance load, kneel or stand on the machine platform, and take a pronated shoulder-width grip with the elbows straight. Pull until the chin clears the handles without kicking or leaning, then lower under control while the platform guides the body vertically.

name: Assisted Chin-Up Machine
movementDefinition: Set the assistance load, kneel or stand on the guided platform, and take a supinated shoulder-width grip with the elbows straight. Pull until the chin clears the handles without kicking or leaning, then lower under control to the starting position.

name: Cable Lat Pulldown
movementDefinition: Sit at a cable pulldown station with the thighs secured beneath the pad and take a medium pronated grip. Keep the trunk braced and nearly upright, pull the bar in front of the head toward the upper chest by driving the elbows down, then return overhead under control.

name: Close-Grip Neutral Lat Pulldown
movementDefinition: Sit with the thighs secured beneath the pad and hold a close parallel-grip attachment with the palms facing each other. Keep the torso braced, drive the elbows down as the handle travels in front of the head toward the upper chest, and return overhead under control.

name: Underhand Lat Pulldown
movementDefinition: Sit with the thighs secured beneath the pad and take a shoulder-width supinated grip on the bar. Hold the trunk nearly upright, drive the elbows down and back as the bar travels in front of the head toward the upper chest, then return overhead under control.

name: Wide-Grip Lat Pulldown
movementDefinition: Sit with the thighs secured beneath the pad and take a wide pronated grip. Keep the trunk braced and nearly upright, pull the bar in front of the head by driving the elbows down until the bar approaches the upper chest, then return overhead under control.

name: Single-Arm Cable Lat Pulldown
movementDefinition: Sit with the thighs secured beneath the pad and hold one high-cable handle in a neutral grip. Keep the shoulders and pelvis square, drive the working elbow down beside the ribs without rotating or leaning, then return the arm overhead under control.

name: Machine Lat Pulldown
movementDefinition: Sit in the lever pulldown machine with the thighs secured beneath the pad and take the neutral handles overhead. Keep the torso braced, drive both elbows down as the levers follow their guided path, and return to full overhead reach under control.

name: Single-Arm Machine Lat Pulldown
movementDefinition: Sit in the independent-arm lever pulldown machine with the thighs secured and hold one neutral handle overhead. Keep the torso and pelvis square, drive the working elbow down without rotating or leaning, and return the lever overhead under control.

name: Seated Barbell Reverse Wrist Curl
movementDefinition: Sit astride a flat bench with both pronated forearms supported and the wrists extending just beyond the edge. Hold a straight bar without opening the fingers, extend both wrists through the controlled available range, and lower under control without rotating the forearms or moving the elbows, shoulders, or torso.

name: Seated Barbell Wrist Curl
movementDefinition: Sit astride a flat bench with both supinated forearms supported and the wrists extending just beyond the edge. Hold a straight bar without opening the fingers, flex both wrists through the controlled available range, and lower under control without rotating the forearms or moving the elbows, shoulders, or torso.

name: Standing Dumbbell Radial Deviation
movementDefinition: Stand tall with the working arm beside the torso, the elbow extended, and the thumb pointing forward. Grip below the dumbbell's bottom collar with its shaft pointing ahead, raise the thumb side of the wrist through the controlled available range, and lower without rotating the forearm or moving the elbow, shoulder, or torso.

name: Standing Dumbbell Ulnar Deviation
movementDefinition: Stand tall with the working arm beside the torso, the elbow extended, and the thumb pointing forward. Grip just above the dumbbell's bottom collar with its shaft pointing behind, raise the little-finger side of the wrist through the controlled available range, and lower without rotating the forearm or moving the elbow, shoulder, or torso.
